title: The Great Panjandrum
caption:
Britain strapped rockets to a giant wheel of explosives and hoped it would roll in a straight line. It did not. 🎡💥
Rockets on both rims had to push equally: when one side's rockets failed, the lopsided push turned the wheel toward the side still firing.
Genius weapon ahead of its time, or the worst idea of the war?
first_comment: Somewhere a 1943 engineer said 'what if a bomb, but it does donuts' and got funding 🍩🚀
sources: Imperial War Museums film records and Wikipedia 'Panjandrum': designed 1943 by the Admiralty's Directorate of Miscellaneous Weapons Development; two 10 ft (3 m) wheels with a central drum carrying about 4,000 lb (~1.8 t) of explosive, driven by cordite rockets on the rims; never used in action

Westward Ho! trials (Devon, January 1944): during the final demonstration rockets broke loose, the wheel veered toward the cameraman (Louis Klemantaski) and onlookers took cover behind the pebble ridge (Wikipedia 'Panjandrum'; The Past, 'Back to the drawing board: the Great Panjandrum')
